newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Busang ore samples said to be tested next week.
newsitem.headline: Busang ore samples said to be tested next week.

text.p: Laboratory testing on ore samples obtained from the controversial Busang gold property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan is expected to begin next week, a spokeswoman for the Busang partners said on Thursday.
"The samples are scheduled to be sent to three laboratories for testing by the end of this week," said Nia Sarinastiti, spokeswoman for the Busang Indonesian Gold JV consortium.
"The samples will be escorted by security personnel from London hired by Strathcona," she told Reuters.
Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services has been hired by Bre-X Minerals Ltd to conduct an independent audit to determine the amount of gold in the Busang property.

Bre-X shocked the mining community last month by admitting there was a possibility the amount of gold at Busang had been overstated. It had earlier put gold reserves at 70.95 million ounces, which would have made it the century's biggest find.

Bre-X has a 45 percent stake in Busang, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States has 15 percent, the Indonesian government 10 percent and the Nusamba Group and its local partner the rest.

Sarinastiti said the 11,795 kg (11.6 tonnes) of ore samples obtained by Strathcona from Busang were being crushed at an undisclosed laboratory in Perth, Australia. The samples were flown there on Tuesday under guard by the British security team.

She said officials from the local mines and energy ministry, who had gone to Perth on Tuesday along with executives from the firms involved in the Busang project, were keen on accompanying the samples when they were flown to the three laboratories.
"The officials would like to do that, but it hasn't been decided yet," she said.
The samples are to be tested at a laboratory belonging to PT Indo Assay in the East Kalimantan town of Balikpapan, and two others in Perth and Vancouver, Canada, Sarinastiti said.
The results are expected in the first week of May, she added.
Officials at Indo Assay refused comment when contacted by Reuters on Thursday.
